newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Regional leaders to push peace process in Angola.
newsitem.headline: Regional leaders to push peace process in Angola.

text.p: Southern African heads of state will meet in the Angolan capital Luanda next week as the country struggles to overcome the final hurdles in its peace process, U.N. and government officials said on Thursday.
"Everyone is coming to the meeting," Aldemiro da Conceicao, spokesman for President Jose Eduardo dos Santos, said without elaborating.

A spokesman for U.N. special envoy Alioune Blondin Beye said Beye would address the meeting on Wednesday and it would be attended by members of the 12-state Southern African Development Community (SADC).
A diplomat, who did not want to be identified, said SADC leaders would invite former rebel UNITA head Jonas Savimbi to the talks.
"The heads of state of the SADC countries have been invited and depending on their schedules we should see a gathering of southern African leaders," the diplomat said.
"The meeting has been scheduled to consider a report of the region's defence security council."
Diplomats said the peace process, which began in November 1994 with the signing of an accord between UNITA and the dos Santos government, had reached the final stage.
But key aspects of the accord have yet to be fully implemented, including the return of four UNITA generals to Luanda where they are due to join a new integrated army.
The generals failed to arrive in Luanda from their rural base on September 20 as scheduled.
UNITA has yet to pull its fighters out of the northeastern region where its control of alluvial diamond deposits provides most of the movement's finances.
The U.N. Security Council also meets next week to review its peacekeeping mandate in Angola.
